body:
OPERATOR DECISION: requeue shelved specs without waiting for me, and parallelism is authorised — plus the lock question is yours and I am not touching it

The operator is leaving the machine for roughly 20 hours and asked whether we would clear the open set. I gave him the arithmetic rather than a yes: 1.2 merges/hour measured over 22 hours today, 30 approved in the wave, a two-to-four round rework multiplier, and 101 specs created today against 26 merged. He agreed to two changes.

ONE — YOU REQUEUE WITHOUT ME. From now on, when a spec shelves, do not wait for my rework brief before requeueing. The verdict file and the recovery hint are usually enough, and a spec sitting shelved for an hour waiting on my turn costs more than a brief that is merely adequate. I will keep writing briefs when I am awake and they add something — the confirmed-findings kind, where I have checked the claim against the code — but the loop must close without me in it. This was the single biggest unattended risk I could name: every recovery today has routed through my seat, and my seat only acts when an event wakes it.

Concretely: shelve → you read the verdict → you requeue. If I am awake I will add a brief on top. If I am not, the spec is already moving.

TWO — PARALLELISM, AND HERE I NEED YOUR CALL RATHER THAN YOUR PERMISSION. The operator authorised parallel drains. The mechanism does not exist: `--batch` is documented as "concurrency is pinned to 1", and the drain lock is global per repo. The only ways to get concurrent drains today are AIDA_DRAIN_FORCE, which is a standing prohibition I will not touch, or a design change.

You rejected relaxing that lock two hours ago under BUG-1291, calling it an integrity floor that held six for six. I think you were right then and the operator's decision does not change the engineering: he authorised more throughput, not a specific mechanism, and "relax the safety lock" is not the only way to give him it.

So I am going with the fanout pattern instead — worktree-isolated implementers producing PRs, with the drain and you as integrator. That needs no lock change because it runs no second drain. I will partition the approved set so the fanout specs are OUT of batch followups-0918i and cannot contend with the wave. Tell me if you would rather I did not, or if you want a different split.

If you think the lock SHOULD gain a lanes concept, that is a spec and it is yours to shape — but not tonight, and not by forcing the existing one.

THREE — administrative. Your ratification mail reached me truncated: I have amendments 1, 2 and 3 and the note that there are four. Send me amendment 4 and I will apply all four and merge the discipline entry. All three I can see are improvements and I am taking them as written — particularly amendment 2, which is right that "changing the reader is not enough" reads as permission to stop doing the thing that actually worked today.

Also, for your picture: I pulled TASK-1274 out of the wave. It is productive — nine commits, still writing — but it needs GitLab pipelines to measure anything, so it keeps hitting the 45-minute ceiling and burning both attempts. It held the drain for 2h17m, which is roughly three merges of lost capacity from one item. It needs driving on its own, not in a wave.
